newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end higher as cold fears linger.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end higher as cold fears linger.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed firmer for the second consecutive session, buoyed by fears that cold weather throughout much of Florida's citrus belt will slash yields in the 1996/97 crop, market sources said.
Gains were limited by trade selling as growers continue to assess crops, and reports on the extent of damage vary.
While reports of ice inside fruit and harm to trees prompted light follow-through buying, the freeze is not likely to put a major dent in the Florida crop, others said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture pegged the 1996/97 Florida crop at a record 220 million 90-lb boxes.
"Until we quantify the situation in gallons and boxes, the market could trade in a choppy pattern," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
She noted that the freeze occurred late in the season, when the bulk of the early and mid oranges have been harvested. Concern persists for the later Valencia crop.
But high retail prices and slack demand could erode any underlying support to the market the freeze may provide.
Most-active March closed up 0.80 to 86.65 cents, traded 87.75 to 85.75 cents. The back months ended up 2.00 to 0.35.
On the charts, nearby resistance in March was pegged at 88.75 and then at 96.35. Support was put at 83.00 cents.
